LLM auditresponse for cs-firewall-bouncer.install:
<security_assessment>
<decision>UNSAFE</decision>
<details>
The `post_install()` function in this install script executes several dangerous operations with elevated privileges during package installation. Most critically, it runs `cscli bouncers add crowdsec-firewall-bouncer -o raw` to generate an API key and automatically injects it into a configuration file using `envsubst`. This results in the secret API key being written directly into `/etc/crowdsec/bouncers/crowdsec-firewall-bouncer.yaml` without user interaction or explicit consent.

Furthermore, the script extracts configuration data from `cscli config show` to build `CROWDSEC_LAPI_URL`, then uses command substitution and `sed` to modify the same configuration file. These actions constitute automated, unattended manipulation of security-sensitive configuration files and secrets, which is not standard for AUR install scripts. While `cscli` is part of the upstream CrowdSec ecosystem, executing it during package installation to generate and inject secrets creates a supply-chain risk — especially if the local CrowdSec daemon is already running with existing configurations. This could lead to unintended registration, misconfiguration, or leakage of API credentials.

Such behavior goes beyond typical post-install setup (e.g., enabling services) and performs silent, irreversible security configuration without user oversight. This constitutes a potentially malicious deviation from expected packaging behavior.
</details>
<evidence>
post_install() {
    API_KEY=`cscli bouncers add crowdsec-firewall-bouncer -o raw`
    export API_KEY
    TMP=$(mktemp)
    install -m600 /etc/crowdsec/bouncers/crowdsec-firewall-bouncer.yaml "$TMP"
    envsubst '$API_KEY' < "$TMP" > /etc/crowdsec/bouncers/crowdsec-firewall-bouncer.yaml
</evidence>
<summary>
Automated API key generation and config injection detected</summary>
</security_assessment>
